installer: KagiR27-2 acting as kaidoku r24 L1, before claim freeze

wireshark.signature_check: gpg --verify in a throwaway GNUPGHOME after --recv-keys 5A5ADBA7DBEA6C3F87224F1982244A78E6FEAEEA from keys.openpgp.org: Good signature from Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>, key not certified by a trusted signature (no web-of-trust path); SHA256 line for the tarball equals source_sha256

build.channel: official source release built locally (no pacman transaction; pacman pause respected)
build.cmake: cmake 4.4.4 via `uv tool install cmake` (PyPI wheel)

libraries_added_after_residual_review.note: Dissector code lives in libwireshark; system libraries come from the host's pacman packages and are not pinned here. A replaced library, or any other TShark 4.x at the configured path, would not by itself cause an REA refusal; only a missing/unrunnable tool does.

wireshark.signature_anchor_limit: The signing key was fetched from keys.openpgp.org; no independent anchor for its fingerprint (e.g. a wireshark.org key page) was recorded this round, so 'signature-checked' means a good signature from that keyserver key, nothing stronger.
wireshark.limits: Binary digests identify this local build only; they are not reproducible-build claims. Lua disabled, so Lua dissectors/plugins are absent from inspect-packet-fields registrations.

capture_inputs.carrier: test/captures/ inside the wireshark-4.6.9.tar.xz above (good signature, see signature_anchor_limit); each capture's own sha256 is recorded in its run/envelope subject digest
capture_inputs.reproduce: curl -fsSLO <source_url>; sha256sum -c; tar xf; files under wireshark-4.6.9/test/captures/
